newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mondale, MOF minister agree on insurance deadline.
newsitem.headline: Mondale, MOF minister agree on insurance deadline.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka reaffirmed their commitment on Thursday to resolving a bilateral dispute over Japan's domestic insurance market by the December 15 deadline, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference.

"Ambassador Mondale and the finance minister have reaffirmed their commitment to resolving the issue by the deadline although both nations have difficult problems," Ogawa said. They also talked about proposed reforms of Japan's financial system, Ogawa said.
Mondale, who is due to retire from his post on December 15, paid a courtesy call to Mitsuzuka earlier on Thursday.
Japan and the United States will resume negotiations on Friday in San Francisco over their insurance dispute, which has become a major trade irritant between the two countries.
They had originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute but agreed to postpone that to December 15. The United States is pressing Japan to open up its primary insurance markets.
Ogawa did not disclose any more details of the meeting.
